# Section 050: Multi-Tenancy Resources

The reader shares one cluster fairly: each tenant namespace gets a quota and default container resources, and priorities decide which pods run when the cluster is full. It comes last because it combines requests, placement and cost into rules for many teams.

**Curriculum item covered:** Optimizing Multi-Tenancy Resource Usage

---

## What You Will Master

- Cap a namespace's total CPU and memory requests and limits and object counts with a ResourceQuota
- Read used against hard in kubectl describe resourcequota
- Diagnose a pod or ReplicaSet rejected by a quota from the Forbidden message and the ReplicaSet events
- Set default requests and limits and per-container minimum and maximum with a LimitRange
- Explain why a compute quota requires every new pod to declare requests, and how a LimitRange default solves that
- Create PriorityClasses and assign them to pods with priorityClassName
- Observe a higher-priority pod preempt lower-priority pods on a full node and read the Preempted events
- Prevent preemption by a class with preemptionPolicy Never
- Limit how much of a namespace's quota high-priority pods may use with a PriorityClass scopeSelector
- Count only BestEffort or Terminating pods with quota scopes

---

## The Learning Path

### 1. Bound Tenants With ResourceQuota And LimitRange
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Bound Tenants With ResourceQuota And LimitRange](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-050/module-01/playground` — Single-node kind cluster. Namespaces `starfleet` and `outpost`, each with `scout` and `shuttle`. `outpost` has a `probe` Deployment without resources. No ResourceQuota or LimitRange, so the reader first sees an unbounded tenant and then adds the limits.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-050/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Share Capacity With PriorityClasses And Quota Scopes
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Share Capacity With PriorityClasses And Quota Scopes](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-050/module-02/playground` — Three-node kind cluster (one control plane, two workers; note the extra memory cost). Namespaces `starfleet` and `outpost`. `outpost` runs `probe` replicas with large requests that fill the workers' allocatable CPU, so a new pod cannot fit. A `scout-critical` Deployment manifest is ready to apply. No PriorityClasses except the built-in system classes, and no ResourceQuota.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-050/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Multi-Tenancy Resources Capstone — `sections/section-050/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-050/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** Two tenants share a small cluster. The reader gives `outpost` a ResourceQuota and a LimitRange so its pods get default requests and cannot exceed its share, creates a PriorityClass so `starfleet`'s `scout` can preempt `outpost` batch pods but `outpost` cannot preempt anyone, and limits high-priority usage with a scoped quota, proving each with admission errors, quota usage and preemption events.
